Latest Update: After GTA 6's original soundtrack, Justice probably won't work on any other video game ever again

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (495 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer.
  • Sources indicate that from what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City.
  • Sources indicate that via a latest interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer. Featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and the fantastic King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, it's clear that the duo - and Rockstar - have spared no expense on the production of music for the game.

Sources indicate that from what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City. You ought to enjoy the music while you can, though, because it seems Justice won't be coming back to video games any time soon. If ever.

Sources indicate that via a latest interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project. "When [the offer to work with Rockstar] arrived on the table, we thought 'if there’s one video game we have to do, it's this one.' As soon as we accepted and started working [on the OST], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game.".

Industry observers note that interesting. The duo, from the clip we can see on Rockyrama's posts, don't seem to give more information about this decision - did they have a bad time working with Rockstar? Was it intense? Or is it rather down to the fact that, if you're going to work on a game, you may as well make it what is largely expected to be the biggest game of all time.

It has been revealed that justice, for what it's worth, consider the work they've done on GTA 6 to be "a real album" of music - it's not seen as lesser or different to the band, just because it's being released as part of a video game. "GTA 6 gave us the excuse and direction to do it. The music always had to be listenable on its own, even if each track is tailored for [a specific] scene," the band explains.

The band's album isn't the only music connected to the game, either. There's also a 34-song album launching for the game, composed of original songs from some of the biggest artists in the world. The album features Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson and many more. The full tracklist leaked at the weekend.

GTA 6 introduces on Thursday, 19th November for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week.

Latest Update: Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (460 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony.
  • As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.
  • The lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the tech giant of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

The lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

It's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

In a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

As if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

Every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another massive game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

Latest Update: From scoffing chips to Snapmatic sh*tposts, GTA 6 is filled with brilliant little details

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1928 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that GTA 6 might only have been with us for a few days, but it's clear from the jump that the level of detail in Rockstar's open world is astonishing.
  • Barely three hours in, GTA 6's reputation system was something I was still getting my head around, but it was already impressing me.
  • They say art imitates life, and that's never been truer than seeing Jason Duval take every opportunity to stuff his face and become a munch goblin in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that GTA 6 might only have been with us for a few days, but it's clear from the jump that the level of detail in Rockstar's open world is astonishing. So I asked the GamesRadar+ team to document their favorite little features that might escape your attention if you're not looking very closely. From turn-signals to hyper-efficient snacking techniques, and social media to road condition, here's what impressed us the most in our opening few days.

Barely three hours in, GTA 6's reputation system was something I was still getting my head around, but it was already impressing me. In an early mission where I went to collect rent money for Brian, the store owner got mad at me and pulled a baseball bat. Before he could rush me, I pulled out Jason's pistol and he balked at just the sight of the gun, dropping the bat and agreeing to hand over the payment. I love that the game logged that as an illegal activity, but still one that showed restraint, heightening Jason's reputation as a cool, collected, professional criminal. It's a nuance that few RPGs capture so effectively, and I'm looking forward to how it works over the rest of the game.

Oscar Taylor-Kent, games editor.

They say art imitates life, and that's never been truer than seeing Jason Duval take every opportunity to stuff his face and become a munch goblin in GTA 6. Like when I do it, it's to obtain buffs to my health, stamina, and focus, of course. Choking out police security, I take time to pour myself a mug of java, sipping it as I slink behind cover. After a stressful interaction with a neighbour, I double fist her endless fruit bowl as I crunch apples and leave the cores around her kitchenette. The detail is tremendous – with one hand carrying a crate of beer, Jason will open potato chips one-handed with his mouth before pouring a few bites at a time into his beard-framed mouth. That's my move. I couldn't be prouder.

Jasmine Gould-Wilson, Senior Staff Writer.

In a recent development, I have a very particular problem with GTA 6's hyper-realistic car damage mechanics. Specifically, they are so realistic that it makes me panic to even be in my car. The slightest ding against a post box results in an ugly dent in the side of my freshly-painted truck, and don't get me started on how bit of bumper-to-bumper action with another car while squeezing my way onto the highway means an unsightly horizontal scrape all down my… whatever part of the car my door is on. I'm not a cars person, okay? I suck at driving in video games and don't even have my license in the real world (partially because I suck at driving in video games). Yet GTA 6 has me feeling incredibly precious about my ride looking beautiful, and I can't stop visiting every pay and spray in town to address even the tiniest nicks of cosmetic damage.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Catherine Lewis, deputy news editor.

It has been revealed that rockstar has managed to craft a jaw-droppingly realistic world in GTA 6, with gorgeous scenery rich in details that make Leonida feel like a lived-in place. But it's not the graphics that have left me most impressed – it's the devs' attention to detail with the many hilarious Snapmatic shitposts. The in-universe take on Instagram is full of photos and videos from the various residents of Leonida, but the highlights are the ridiculous memes that wouldn't look at all out of place on real-life social media. From "Taco Bomb made me shid my pant" to "do nothing for two hours or straight jork it," an image outside a nursing home captioned "POV: grandma insulted my 6'7 fem-dom goth milk mommy," and Rockstar even parodying the "we got x before GTA 6" memes, I've spent more time scrolling social media in the game over the last day than I have in real life – and, uh, that's saying something. Jason's algorithm is absurd and deeply cursed, and I'm loving it.

Sources indicate that I've spent about four hours with GTA 6 so far, and for most of that time, I've been driving. As a bonafide car sicko when it comes to video games, Rockstar's latest is already making my heart go pitter patter. Why? Because I can actually use my car blinkers to indicate when I'm making a turn with the DPad on my PS5 controller. It might sound mundane, but this is a Substantial Deal to me. It's something I could only dream of when I was cruising around Vice City back in the day, or getting behind the wheel in GTA 5. I've always been one to obey traffic laws in the series, and you better believe I've been stopping at red lights and making way for passing cars. And now I can also indicate each and every turn like a good citizen should? I'm living the dream. What's more, the indicator even automatically switches off when I make my desired turn like a real car. Be still my car-loving heart.

Industry observers note that there's a moment in the first chapter where it's time for a party at a local bar, a well-earned celebration in the wake of some good news. Normally this is the sort of thing in a game that'd have me checking my watch and wondering when I can go back to shooting people, but Rockstar's strong writing and character work turn what might've felt like a filler sequence into a moment for developing relationships and story alike (something I can't yet say about the grocery shopping mechanics). But what stuck out for me is just how real it all felt: that one asshole showing up that everybody regrets inviting, the way that people join and split and converge in different groups, the natural rise and fall of energy across the evening. It all ends with a pleasingly solid pool minigame, interrupted by some belligerent drunks who actually snatched my ball off the table as I was about to pot the winning shot, damn it. Alright, now I'm ready to shoot people again.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 may be full of thrilling violence and satirical comedy, but my favorite feature so far is its life-sim management elements. Playing as Jason, there's plenty of opportunity to carry out more mundane activities, and the rewards are deeply gratifying. Ahead of Lucia's release from prison, you can repair your home, buy flowers and groceries, and even order a gold necklace to show her how much Jason cares. Lucia's dialogue conveys the character's appreciation, which is nice enough on its own, but the simple act of doing these things also feels good in the moment. Watching Jason roll paint on bare bedroom walls and affix shingles to a leaking roof is soothing, and adds to the sense of immersion because we see the protagonist committing acts of affection that feel real and relatable. I love stealing cars and generally causing mayhem, but I equally enjoy living out more wholesome fantasies in Leonida, and I implore you to do the same.

One of the biggest changes you'll notice in GTA 6 compared to GTA 5 is the ability to choose. Each mission gives you an objective to complete and lets you decide how to do it. Some early-game errands, like rent collection, can get dirty if you really want, though you can also talk people out of making the dumb decision. It's a fresh change that not only takes GTA 6 to the next level but also lets you shape Jason into who you want him to be. I spend my time outside missions being a chill wife guy who fixes up the house and runs errands – so why let a scripted mission run counter to that? My Jason didn't pick that life; it picked him and he's just trying to make it through the best he can.

Scott McCrae, Freelance Contributor.

Recent findings suggest that obviously there's so much talk about how much of a lived-in world Rockstar Games has created, but one of the ways this has most stuck out to me is through the use of music. Early on I had to head to an artists market to collect some cash from one of Brian's many clientele, but as I parked my car and wandered through the market and heard Elton John's 'I Guess That's Why They Call It The Blues' playing in the distance on a speaker, so instead of immediately walking in to shake down the acid-dealing hippie, I just sort of hung about to listen. I've loved walking into stores to hear a banger playing on their radio, or hanging around areas like that where what song plays gives you a good idea of what the area's culture is like. Perhaps the best use so far has been in the party scene (mentioned above by Joel) where the local band shows up, but instead of just playing licensed music to simulate it, you hear actual covers of classics like Out of Touch by Hall and Oates, to really drive home that local bar feeling.

I've visited Florida quite a bit over the years, but not as a typical tourist. Much of my time there has been spent driving to visit friends who live among the state's smaller towns, and GTA 6 does an incredible job of showcasing just how awful the local roads are. State highways patched over with mismatched blacktop and concrete? Check. Bizarre turn lanes that appear and disappear without a second to get your bearings? Double check. Hastily paved entrances into strip malls that feel like they're going to destroy your car's suspension? Triple check. Leonida has enough similarities to real-life Florida to send a normal driver to a life of crime.

It has been revealed that on my Leonida travels, I found a cow that spoke to me. Yes, that sounds insane but I promise it really happened. A runaway pageant cow called Tootsie, dressed in an elaborate red cover, with red bows tied around her ankles, and a fancy flowery hat, made for the hills, leaving me to help the farmer bring her back. I eventually caught up to Tootsie and calmed her down, but then she uttered a chilling "save me". Like Jason, I also physically recoiled at this. I was unsettled for the entire walk back to the farmer, Tootsie now back to regular mooing. Rather than helping the farmer load her into the trailer, I instead shooed Tootsie away, sending her into the sunset. The farmer was - unsurprisingly - livid, saying she wouldn't make it in the wild. I've not seen Tootsie again but I hope she's doing alright.

I'm GamesRadar's Managing Editor for news, shaping the news strategy across the team. I started my journalistic career while getting my degree in English Literature at the University of Warwick, where I also worked as Games Editor on the student newspaper, The Boar. Since then, I've run the news sections at PCGamesN and Kotaku UK, and also regularly contributed to PC Gamer. As you might be able to tell, PC is my platform of choice, so you can regularly find me playing League of Legends or Steam's latest indie hit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, upgrading your TV's sound doesn't necessarily mean spending a fortune on a full home theater setup, especially with early Black Friday deals bringing substantial discounts on soundbars and audio systems from Sony, Bose, Samsung, and LG. Sony has some of the biggest price cuts, with savings of up to 32% across select Bravia Theater models, including more than $700 off its premium Theater Trio system.

Samsung's Dolby Atmos soundbars are also discounted by as much as $400, while Bose and LG have more affordable options for anyone looking to improve dialogue clarity, add some bass, or enjoy surround sound without a complicated setup. Whether you're shopping for a compact speaker for a bedroom TV or a more immersive system for movie nights, here are the deals worth considering.

In a recent development, for anyone building a premium home theater around a large TV, the Sony Bravia Theater Trio is down to $1,498 from $2,199.99, saving you $701.99, or roughly 32%. Unlike a conventional soundbar, the Trio uses three separate front speakers for the left, center, and right channels, helping spread dialogue and effects across a wider soundstage. You can read PCMag’s “excellent” review for more details.

The Sony Bravia Theater Bar 7 is down to $718 from $869 for anyone who wants a single soundbar under the TV. Its nine speakers include upward- and side-firing drivers that widen the soundstage and give Dolby Atmos some height, but there’s no subwoofer, so the now $898 Bar 7 with a wireless sub bundle (down from $1,099.99) might be the better pick for deeper bass.

It has been revealed that moving down Sony's lineup, the Bravia Theater Bar 6 is $548, down from $699.99, and pairs a 3.1.2-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer and upward-firing speakers for Dolby Atmos height effects. Spending $100 more gets you the Bravia Theater System 6, now $648 from $799.99, which adds rear speakers in a 5.1-channel setup for movies and games where sound moves behind you.

It has been revealed that for a more affordable upgrade, the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 5 is down to $278 from $349.99, saving you nearly $72. It's a 3.1-channel system with a dedicated center speaker and wireless subwoofer, so dialogue should come through more clearly while music and movie effects get some additional low-end presence.

Sources indicate that sony’s older systems are discounted too, including the HT-S400 at $258, down from $299, which pairs a 2.1-channel soundbar and wireless subwoofer with S-Force Pro Front Surround to widen the sound for everyday TV, sports, and casual movies. The HT-S40R is arguably the better deal at the same $258, down from $329.99, since it adds two rear speakers for a full 5.1-channel setup, though neither model supports Dolby Atmos.

Recent findings suggest that for smaller rooms or for anyone who mainly wants dialogue to come across more clearly, Bose has two compact soundbars on sale: The newer Bose TV Speaker (2nd Gen) is down to $239 from $299, with an updated acoustic design that Bose states improves clarity and overall sound performance. Meanwhile, the original Bose TV Speaker is $199, down from $279, and offers a similarly compact design with a dedicated dialogue mode and adjustable bass.

In a recent development, samsung’s HW-Q800H is down to $697.99 from $1,097.99, a $400 cut on a 5.1.2-channel Dolby Atmos soundbar with a wireless subwoofer. Its side- and upward-firing speakers help place effects around and above you, while a dedicated center channel keeps dialogue clear during busy action scenes.

For something that takes up less space, the Samsung HW-S60D is $277.99, down from $399.99, and fits seven speakers, including side-firing drivers, into a compact 5.0-channel soundbar. It also supports Dolby Atmos, Adaptive Sound, and a voice enhancement mode, along with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, AirPlay, and Chromecast for music streaming. That remarked, it has no upward-firing speakers or subwoofer, so its height effects and bass won’t match that of the Q800H.

In a recent development, if you're looking for a complete surround sound system without spending several hundred dollars, the LG S6FTR is down to $249.99 from $399.99, saving you $150, or roughly 38%. It's a 5.1-channel home theater package with a soundbar, subwoofer, and dedicated rear speakers. That makes it particularly appealing for action movies and games, where directional sound adds to the experience.

The LG S40TR is another affordable option for anyone who wants rear speakers included in the box. It's currently $199.99, down from $279.99, and offers a 4.1-channel arrangement with a wireless subwoofer and two rear speakers. This should give movie soundtracks a greater sense of direction than a basic soundbar, while the subwoofer handles the lower frequencies that smaller TV speakers often struggle to reproduce.

At just under $187, the S60T is the least expensive system in this roundup, pairing a 3.1-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer for clearer dialogue and fuller sound than your TV’s speakers. That remarked, it lacks rear speakers and Dolby Atmos height channels, so it’s better suited to someone who wants a simple, affordable upgrade without filling the room with additional hardware.

In a recent development, in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

According to recent reports, black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February.
  • Industry observers note that this promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies.
  • In a recent development, in addition, there's an alluring character skip available too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February. So, in order to keep the game populated for the next few months, Square Enix is running a special promotion in hopes of tempting players back in.

Industry observers note that this promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies. Lapsed players who haven't logged in for over six months are to be given 30 days of free game time to hop back in and catch up with the main story quest ahead of Evercold's release.

In a recent development, in addition, there's an alluring character skip available too. If your FF14 character is at least level 90 on one class - the current level-cap is 100 - you can skip all the way to the final part of the latest Dawntrail expansion. You still need to grind to level 100 in preparation for Evercold, but the aforementioned free month of game time should provide plenty of time to do so.

In a producer letter written to accompany this promotion, Naoki Yoshida provided insight into why this was being implemented, stating that retaining players in an MMO like FF14 was of the "utmost importance".

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat", Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

"For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn debuted, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today.".

Yoshida went on to explain that promotions such as this are meant as a "tiny nudge". He notes that those who have retained subscriptions continuously remain "the most key" players in the development team's eyes, and acknowledges that the process of catching up in an MMO can seem "daunting" for many.

It has been revealed that this problem of player retention is nothing upcoming for MMOs, especially in the tricky time between the end of a current expansion and the beginning of a new one. MMO popularity often waxes and wanes, with a new expansion acting as an exciting call to action, with the months leading up to it often serving as a natural break-point for many. Still, monthly subs pay the bills, so keeping folks around even during these quiet months is important.

Final Fantasy 14: Evercold is looking like an especially exciting expansion. On top of the new story and two classes being added, the game is getting an overhaul to combat, with both classic Reborn and Evolved action modes, as well as a new raid difficulty meant to bridge the gap between normal and savage tiers.

Sources indicate that the game has certainly come a long way since its initial release back in 2010. Dawntrail proved divisive among fans too, though with Evercold there's a lot of hope that a upcoming overarching storyline can bring the steal back the hearts of players old and new.

Recent findings suggest that upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

According to recent reports, word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

Recent findings suggest that "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a manufacturer succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

GTA 6 has been updated to support PS Plus Premium cloud streaming directly to the PS5 and PS Portal.

To be crystal clear about this: the game has not been added to the PS Plus Premium catalogue and you will still need to own it.

However, assuming you’ve purchased the game – and millions of you have – then you’ll now be able to stream it directly from Sony’s servers, assuming you’re a PS Plus Premium member.

There are a number of use cases for this, but the most likely is you’re away from your console and still want to play on your PS Portal. Now you won’t need to rely on Remote Play; you can just stream it directly.

This feature wasn’t available at launch, but I’ve been able to test it on my PS5 here in the UK and it’s working well.

There was some reporting prior to release that Microsoft had secured “exclusive” streaming rights to this title, but they were promptly clarified. This update now confirms boss Asha Sharma misspoke.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood.

I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN, Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom.

"A massive part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer.".

Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this substantial machine is always running even when players aren't there.".

Recent findings suggest that while this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. But it's such commitment to representing its world that has led GTA 6 to receive near-universal praise from critics, and it probably didn't hurt when it earned $3.79 billion on launch day, either.

#166257. What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1690 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1690 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto.
  • Industry observers note that it wasn't ever thus.
  • During the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

Industry observers note that it wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

During the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross Fresh York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

According to recent reports, in amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far.".

The pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something new," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty promptly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died.".

The increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The big project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again.".

Rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA.".

Industry observers note that agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished.".

While never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij remarked. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched.".

In a recent development, as for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij said, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

Recent findings suggest that needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them.".

In a recent development, according to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

One thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

According to recent reports, "I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

Recent findings suggest that "At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death. The mangaka, whose art and distinct style were foundational to Chrono Trigger and Chrono Cross - and are still used in Dragon Quest to this day - died in 2024 at the age of 68.

According to recent reports, today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something fresh. This was all triggered by the announcement of Dragon Quest RPG: The Island of the Demon Tree and the Guided Island, an iOS and Android game that uses art that is very reminiscent of Toriyama's.

According to recent reports, "The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," said Mitsuda. "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly new no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end for now, and [Dragon Quest creator, Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG. (There have been many remakes already.)".

Sources indicate that horii himself seems undeterred: with the new mobile game's announcement last week, he noted that the goal of his new project is to "capture that unmistakable Dragon Quest feeling" that comes with "exploring towns, meeting new allies, gearing up and steadily growing stronger". As Mitsuda calls for the series to retire, and for something new to take its place, Horii is keen to bring "the same classic adventure" to your smartphone.

"What's important is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future," concluded Mitsuda. "But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people.".

It's unlikely Square Enix is going to want to drop the series, of course: the Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake exceeded Square Enix's (in)famously lofty expectations, and as the firm aggressively pursues its multiplatform strategy, it's hard to imagine a world in which it's going to want to move away from a series that routinely pulls in millions of sales.

Call of Duty might have swapped guns and tanks for knights and swords if an Infinity Ward experiment had panned out

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold fresh directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day.
  • Recent findings suggest that this latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game.
  • Industry observers note that this isn't the first time we've heard of an unusual Call of Duty prototype.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold fresh directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day. And it turns out a medieval Call of Duty was also explored at one time.

Recent findings suggest that this latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game. "Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right?" Kurosaki told PC Gamer. "It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty.".

Industry observers note that this isn't the first time we've heard of an unusual Call of Duty prototype. When Activision brought Sledgehammer Games into the fold as another lead studio for the lucrative shooter series, the team briefly worked on a third-person horror off-shoot set in Vietnam, which was referred to as Fog of War.

Activision's legal battle with Infinity Ward founders Vince Zampella and Jason West, however, caused the project to be cancelled, as Sledgehammer was roped into helping the studio finish Modern Warfare 3.

Industry observers note that as for Kurosaki, he presently leads That's No Moon alongside creative partner Jacob Minkoff and other Infinity Ward and Naughty Dog veterans. The studio is currently working on Crossfire, a narrative-driven third-person shooter set in the universe of Smilegate's free-to-play series of the same name.

I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

To top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

In a recent development, it's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With Mass Effect Universe, BioWare was trying its best to account for all the endings of Mass Effect 3 in a way that preserved player choice and narrative impact but still allowed for a new story to be told.
  • It has been revealed that that's according to Mass Effect: Annihilation writer Catherynne M.
  • Valente discusses her work with BioWare in a Reddit AMA held in support of the Save Mass Effect movement, which has seen fans call for BioWare and/or its series to be revived, and which Valente plugs in her post about the AMA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With Mass Effect Universe, BioWare was trying its best to account for all the endings of Mass Effect 3 in a way that preserved player choice and narrative impact but still allowed for a new story to be told.

It has been revealed that that's according to Mass Effect: Annihilation writer Catherynne M. Valente, who worked on Mass Effect Universe before BioWare was shut down and its sci-fi RPG series was put on ice. The Annihilation novel was published in November 2018 as part of the Mass Effect: Andromeda extended universe.

Valente discusses her work with BioWare in a Reddit AMA held in support of the Save Mass Effect movement, which has seen fans call for BioWare and/or its series to be revived, and which Valente plugs in her post about the AMA.

One user asked, "How did you and the rest of the team take the endings into account?" as "each one had pretty wildly different outcomes that are hard to reconcile.".

According to recent reports, not for the first time, Valente explains that many Mass Effect Universe details are still under NDA and cannot be shared, plus the game was very unfinished and details could shift. But she does dig into the general approach BioWare took with this narrative challenge.

"I don't think it's being naughty to say I (and not only me, but I did a lot on it) worked specifically, and for a very long and laborious time, on handling the endings in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off," she says, "at least not piss them off completely, that wouldn't make them feel like nothing mattered, wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another, but also allow us, somehow, to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream video game and not a post-modern 3000 page novel.".

Sources indicate that as you may have deduced, "that's kind of a tall fucking order," as Valente puts it. BioWare had to ride multiple horses at the same time and get them all to gallop in the same direction.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

The search for "an elegant solution that we can do with current game tech, that will be approved by higher-ups, that doesn't take over the whole game and make actually telling a story impossible...it takes a long time, and it's not obvious how best to pull it off when you're the people who bear responsibility for pulling off one of, if not the, hardest nut to crack in game writing," she adds.

Recent findings suggest that valente reflects on the broader fandom surrounding Mass Effect. "It's become really clear that it's impossible to make the gaming community completely happy with anything no matter how hard you try, especially the ME endings that were so controversial, yet people feel so strongly about their own choices," she says.

In a recent development, she dismisses the argument that BioWare can simply make ME3's Destroy ending canon, noting that some players, including her, feel strongly about the Synthesis ending. So the solution BioWare had arrived at, she suggests, was decidedly not singular.

In a recent development, "We did our best, and I think we landed in a good place," she recalls. "There wasn't one single solution, but several working together, and unfortunately I can't say any more than that.".

She does, however, say more than that. Valente examines the role of narrative sin eater in a post-ME3 world. "I remember laughing ruefully once and thinking god, if I'd known when I finished ME3 that I'd be one of the people who had to find the mops and buckets to clean up that mess..." The worst part is that I've always gotten the impression BioWare wasn't gleefully sowing with the ME3 endings even back in the day – it's just reaping all the way down. Always those darn Reapers.

Nevertheless, Valente maintains that BioWare was in a good position to tackle all this. "That room was *full* of ambition and enthusiasm, and I don't think it could have been in better hands," she states. "We knew all the discourse on the endings, of course we did, and I do think as a fan I would have been happy with the solution (at least what it was when I left) if I booted up the game having had nothing to do with it.".

Former Dragon Age lead says EA mismanagement killed BioWare by forcing it into terrible choices: "They made us do something".

It has been revealed that austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible.

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (295 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record.
  • Industry observers note that the remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November).
  • While Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game, Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail.

Industry observers note that the remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom. That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years.

While Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026, and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028.

Industry observers note that ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post, Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if you were having trouble accessing certain services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook, you were not alone.
  • In a recent development, when I first published this article on Thursday, I couldn't even load Microsoft 365's status page.
  • According to recent reports, looking specifically at Outlook, Microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports Thursday afternoon, signaling a major concern somewhere in Microsoft's pipeline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you were having trouble accessing certain services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook, you were not alone. Early Thursday afternoon, many of Microsoft's biggest apps and services were experiencing downtime. According to Downdetector, which tracks user reports of complications with websites and platforms, Microsoft 365, Teams, Copilot, Teams, and OneDrive were all experiencing issues. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft has restored service to many users, and has officially apologized for the outages.

In a recent development, when I first published this article on Thursday, I couldn't even load Microsoft 365's status page. (I've reported on many service outages, but I can't recall a time when a service's status page was also down.) Even as of Friday afternoon, the page still says "Service degradation on Microsoft 365 (Business or Enterprise)," and Microsoft says the following services may be affected: Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center, Microsoft 365 Education, Microsoft Copilot 365, Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Graph, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Planner, Microsoft Power Apps, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft To Do, Power BI, SharePoint Online, Universal Print, and Windows 365.

According to recent reports, looking specifically at Outlook, Microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports Thursday afternoon, signaling a major concern somewhere in Microsoft's pipeline. The reports did "slow down" throughout the day, but Downdetector still showed over 50,000 reports coming in every 15 minutes when I checked Thursday afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that while the root cause of the glitch was a mystery throughout Thursday's outage, Microsoft confirmed the problem in an apology on Friday. According to the company, "This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI [or] agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.".

Recent findings suggest that microsoft claims it is "deeply sorry" for the disruption to its customers and partners. The company says the fix rolled out slower than some might expect, since it wanted to restore service gradually to evaluate stability at each stage. It also says it will release a full post-incident report once it completes a review.

Industry observers note that during the outage, the firm had confirmed that some of its infrastructure was experiencing elevated load, which it noted was likely contributing to the concerns. Microsoft then said it was pausing all deployments and moving traffic from affected infrastructure, and that it found that a number of its servers were unexpectedly unavailable after failing health checks. The company then thought a specific component responsible for processing server health may be the reason the system is failing health checks. Microsoft said an alternative service health check method successfully restarted some of the affected servers. The company was then actively restarting and validating affected servers to bring them back to service.

I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

It has been revealed that everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

The world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You'll have to track down the GTA 6 Riata locations to fix the second Classic Car Collection vehicle for Wyman. He'll text you a little while after you complete the Transgressor, this time sending you to the Key Lento area, unfortunately a rather long drive when you're likely still at the motel near Port Gellhorn.

There are three Riatas you need to scan with the WAiNK It app to fix up this classic off-roading 4x4, one in Key Lento itself, one near the naval base at Goose Key, and a final one in Shoeless Keys.

This is the first one Wyman asks you to find, near the PD in the Keys. It's under a brown stilt house north of Leonida Key Lento Mini-mart and the Shrimp 'n Save, on that northernmost road running through the Key. Find the brown stilt house, as in the video above, then just head underneath to scan the car.

In a recent development, this second one is located in Southwind, on Goose Key, the island with the Mile Zero Air Station to the west of Key Lento—you will have visited here for a mission early in the game. The junked car is under another brown stilt house at the end of the road down to the east from the Xero Gas - Southwind station, on the right just before the sea.

It has been revealed that this third one is located behind the ruined gas station just to the north of Grassrivers Cafe & Deli in Shoeless Keys. The tricky part is that this is a four-star area (because of the final missions in Chapter 1), so you'll want to be quick as otherwise a police chopper will come and spot you. When you turn off the main road, the garage is on your left before you reach the cafe itself, with the car just behind.

Somehow, I forgot to record this one, but I still show the location in the clip above behind the gas station (just without the car since it was gone when I re-recorded).

Once you have all three, Wyman will tell you to wait a little while, and then will call and ask you to Buck him $1,500 for the labour. Select the payment request in the text, or do it manually in the app. A little while after the money is sent, you'll get a map marker for Wyman's scrapyard, where you can pick up this completed classic car.

Just about every veteran developer in the industry has been heaping praise on GTA 6 since its release last week, but I'm not sure any of that rampant positivity matches the thoughts of Igor Sarzynski.

Sarzynski is at the moment the creative director on Cyberpunk 2 (as it's officially known right now), having previously worked on both The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 — two games that are widely considered to be amongst the best that the open world genre has to offer.

In other words, Sarzynski knows what he's talking about when he indicates GTA 6 is "probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history". Now that's praise.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," he noted on social media.

Sources indicate that "Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle.".

"Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled," Sarzynski jokes, suggesting that no one's going to match Rockstar's effort for quite some time. "I'mma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now.".

If you've played GTA 6, you can surely understand why every non-Rockstar developer is looking at it and being left in a state of near disbelief. We're not getting another release like it for years and years to come — and just like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it, it's going to become the benchmark for open world games.

Still, there'll come a time when Cyberpunk 2 takes all the headlines — it's just that right now, it's hard to see beyond GTA 6 because it's absolutely bloody everywhere (and with good reason).

"Seriously though I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavour," Sarzynski continues in a follow-up post.

"GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed," he concludes — and that's pretty much a perfect way to put it.

Industry observers note that do you agree with Sarzynski? Just how big of an achievement do you think GTA 6 really is? Have your mind blown in the comments section below.

  • Recent findings suggest that is the nickname FemJun too blatant?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

Recent findings suggest that is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

There are, however, substantial and crucial differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

Recent findings suggest that archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons company Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Sources indicate that female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

Archetype revealed a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

Industry observers note that matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year.".

Welcome to a brand new week of GTA 6 still blowing everyone's minds. We will probably be covering this beat for months if not years as players and game developers continue unearthing new discoveries and technical marvels, with one prominent dev comparing GTA 6 to the Great Pyramids in Egypt.

Mark Richard Davies, game director at Naughty Dog and game designer on The Last of Us 2, is the latest game developer to appear awe-stricken in reaction to Rockstar's opus. A colleague of Davies, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet world design director Michael Barclay, recently said GTA 6 appears to him "as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child," underscoring the unprecedented depth and scale of the game.

According to recent reports, in a newly introduced tweet, Davies says we might never find every piece of the GTA 6 puzzle and jokingly predicts we'll one day discover extraterrestrial intelligence hiding in its DNA. "GTA VI is the Great Pyramids of Game Development," he says. "As in, people will be asking for centuries how it was possible and we will eventually conclude that aliens made it.".

GTA VI is the Great Pyramids of Game Development. As in, people will be asking for centuries how it was possible and we will eventually conclude that aliens made it.November 22, 2026.

In response to a commenter who rightfully points out Rockstar's "8 to 13" year development cycle and estimated $1 billion budget, Davis simply says, "I'm sure the pyramids were expensive too," seemingly acknowledging that one part of Rockstar's magic is unfathomable financial resources. For instance, the thing that amazes Davies the most about GTA 6, in his words, is "Every NPC having voice lines and reactions. The sheer size of the script must be mind boggling." The level of interactivity and variety in GTA 6's NPCs is hugely immersive, but that wouldn't have been possible if Rockstar and parent company Take-Two Interactive didn't have the money to pay that amount of voice and performance capture artists.

All that said, in addition to lots and lots of money, there's an element to Rockstar's sterling track record for genre-defining releases that has very little to do with money and a lot to do with extremely talented individuals firing on all cylinders and a unified vision from legacy leadership. But, you know, having $1 billion dollars to spend certainly doesn't hurt.

"Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled," notes the RPG's director after entering a "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

Industry observers note that "What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the plans for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely fresh modes, the possibilities are vast.".

The post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a big visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial.".

In a recent development, beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one significant revision sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer
